scene_description: Both images depict a small light-colored living room with a pale blue three-seat sofa and right-side chaise, a central coffee table, a low white unit on the left, a tall white cabinet and floor lamp near the sofa, a tall open shelving unit on the right, wall art, and a framed rectangle above the sofa.

observations: The major furniture and wall objects are present in both images in corresponding positions.
The candidate simplifies the wall art, shelving, mirror-like wall frame, table, and sofa detailing.

The sofa faces the foreground, with its chaise projecting on the viewer's right in both images. The white cabinet stands to its right, the lamp is behind that area, and the open shelving is farther right.
The coffee table is centered in front of the sofa, with the low unit along the left wall. The candidate leaves noticeably more visible floor around the furniture because of its wider composition.
spatial_relations_and_orientation.image_evidence: Reference and candidate, central sofa and surrounding furniture.

observations: The reference sofa occupies a much larger fraction of the frame; the candidate sofa and adjacent furnishings appear smaller and farther away.

The reference shelving is very large and cropped at the right edge, while the candidate shows nearly its full height and more of its side. The candidate table is fully visible horizontally and its legs are exposed, unlike the tightly cropped reference table.
The lamp is partly obscured by the sofa and cabinet in both images.
The reference table top has glossy diagonal brown and light streaks; the candidate has a muted brown surface with thin, regular longitudinal pale stripes.
The reference shelving has a light peach wood-grain appearance; the candidate shelving appears flatter and paler with dark corner accents at shelf intersections.
The reference wall art is a large, mostly dark blue field with irregular pink and yellow shapes; the candidate shows a smaller blue field with a simplified pink and black shape.
The candidate's sofa retains the pale cyan coloring, but looks flatter and more block-like than the softly rounded reference cushions.
materials_and_texture.image_evidence: Reference and candidate table, right shelving, left wall art, and sofa.

observations: Both sofas have three back and seat sections and a right-front chaise extension. The candidate has squarer, more uniformly outlined cushions and thinner exposed legs.
The right shelf in the candidate has prominent dark marks at the shelf joints, not apparent in the reference. Its visible cubbies are narrower and arranged differently in the image.
The framed rectangle above the candidate sofa is a plain gray panel, whereas the reference has a reflective-looking surface and visible interior reflections.
visible_geometry.image_evidence: Reference and candidate sofa, shelving, and framed wall rectangle.

observations: The reference is closer and more immersive, with strong foreground cropping of the coffee table, left unit, art, and shelving. The candidate is framed wider, showing more floor and more complete objects.
The candidate camera looks more directly toward the back wall; the reference has stronger apparent perspective and a more prominent right foreground shelf.

Both scenes are softly lit with pale, low-contrast surfaces. The reference is brighter and warmer with a pink-lavender cast and more pronounced glossy table reflections; the candidate is grayer and more subdued.
Soft shadows beneath and behind furniture are visible in both; exact light sources cannot be established from the images.
lighting_and_shadows.image_evidence: Reference and candidate, floor, walls, and table.

objects_regions.observation: Reference sofa is large in frame, with soft rounded cushions and a right-projecting chaise; candidate equivalent is smaller and boxier at [0.30, 0.41, 0.65, 0.72].
Reference top is cropped at the bottom and has glossy diagonal streaks; candidate [0.36, 0.75, 0.64, 1.0] has straight regular lengthwise stripes and exposed legs.
Reference shelving dominates the right foreground with wood grain; candidate [0.72, 0.01, 1.0, 0.91] is more fully visible, less textured, and has dark joint marks.
Reference art is cropped and has a dark blue field with large irregular pink and yellow forms; candidate [0.14, 0.14, 0.26, 0.54] is smaller and its design is simplified.
Reference frame is partly cropped at the top and has visible reflections; candidate [0.43, 0.14, 0.53, 0.34] is fully visible with a flat gray interior.
The cabinet and lamp occupy the corresponding right-of-sofa area in both, although they appear smaller in the candidate [0.61, 0.26, 0.74, 0.66].
The left-side low white unit is present in both, but the candidate [0.07, 0.63, 0.30, 1.0] shows more of its end and top due to framing.
A pale rounded floor covering is visible around the table in both; its outline is more apparent in the wider candidate view.

most_important_visible_defects: The wider, more distant camera composition changes object scale and removes the reference's strong foreground cropping.
The coffee table surface lacks the reference's glossy diagonal streaked appearance.
The wall art and reflective-looking framed rectangle are substantially simplified.
The foreground shelving differs in apparent scale, texture, visible cubby arrangement, and dark joint details.
uncertainty: The framed rectangle may be a mirror or another reflective surface; its exact function is not certain from RGB alone.
Differences in apparent size and spacing can reflect camera placement or lens as well as geometry; absolute dimensions and true contact cannot be established.
Hidden surfaces and the complete geometry of cropped objects are not observable.
limitations: Assessment is based only on the two supplied rendered images and approximate normalized image coordinates.
No hidden geometry, physical materials, or exact lighting setup was inspected.
